description: Mechanics-15, 2D: the 15 ogbench M7-M10 mazes (every non-empty combination of portals, death, rotating and frozen tiles on the 18x18 dense kr/sg/kb skeleton) on Kimi K3, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. The R1 fixed cell (minimal/image_only/egocentric/zero_shot/stateless, step_by_step, progress_stall_k=30) with context_window=full instead of text_summary_and_last_n. MiniGrid backend (no render block); the same manifest serves the NL and 3D runs through their own run configs.
_note_no_conditions: No conditions key => single (default) cell built from experiment_config overlay. Do NOT add conditions (that would re-enable the sweep).
_note_requires: context_window=full comes from PR #54 (R2 full context). Launching before it is on the launched SHA fails at config load.
_note_model_params: Equal 64k output caps (max_tokens; max_completion_tokens for OpenAI and Kimi K3). Thinking on for all three. Opus 5.5: effort=xhigh, no sampling params, Message Batches API via the lockstep worker (worker_role=lockstep-worker; coordinator STALE_AFTER_SECONDS >= 12600). Kimi K3: always thinks, reasoning_effort=max (Moonshot's default, set explicitly for provenance), no thinking object or sampling params; plain worker on the sync API (Moonshot Batch support for kimi-k3 unverified). GPT-6 Astra: reasoning_effort=xhigh, flex tier, image_detail=high, plain worker (the OpenAI agent has no batch path), spend_cap_usd=160 is a per-process hard stop sized to the uncached 150-steps-per-episode estimate (pair it with an OpenAI project budget). context_window=full resends every prior decision frame each query (history capped by max_history_tokens), so per-episode input grows quadratically with steps: estimate cost before launch.
_note_cost: Measured (worst-case smoke, 483 frames of 576x576 in one request; both providers accepted it): ~470 input tokens per frame (Opus 5.5 229,544 tokens, Kimi K3 223,303), so an episode of N queries sends ~470*N^2/2 input tokens. Per model over 15 mazes: ~17M tokens at ~70 queries/episode, ~79M at 150. With prompt caching each query reads the prior history from cache, writes one step (count_tokens on M10: 477 tokens) and sends a ~548-token tail uncached. Input cost over 15 mazes at ~70 / ~150 queries/episode, cached (uncached in brackets): Opus 5.5 batch ($2/M input, $0.20/M read, $4/M 1h write): ~$7 / ~$23 (~$37 / ~$165). Kimi K3 ($3/M input and 5m write, $0.30/M read): ~$8 / ~$31 (~$55 / ~$247), plus output at $15/M (K3 max effort is the open term). GPT-6 Astra flex ($5/M input, $0.50/M read, 1.25x write), if its image tokens and cache reads match (both unmeasured; image_detail=high): ~$15 / ~$53 (~$92 / ~$411), so spend_cap_usd=160 only stops it on long episodes if caching does not hit. Cached figures assume every query hits; a miss rewrites the whole prefix. Calibrate on M10 (run_config.mechanics_15_2d_calib.json) and re-project before launch.
_note_launch: Launch with difficulty_max_static_score = 8000 (--difficulty-max-static-score 8000, fleet DIFFICULTY_MAX=8000), set for this panel: the largest static score is M10's, about 7,840. Stage 2 refuses the run if any selected maze scores above the cap. Stage 2 takes tens of minutes per maze on these 18x18 mechanics mazes: pre-score with a local coordinator-prepare and launch with PRESCORED_TASKS. Serve the coordinator with STALE_AFTER_SECONDS >= 12600 for the lockstep Opus group.
_note_cache: Prompt caching on (PRs #64/#65): experiment_config.prompt_cache=true with context_window=full marks the newest history step and the previous request's newest step, so each query reads the system prompt and every earlier frame, inventory and action from cache and writes only the new step; the current frame, budget/stall lines and question sit after the last breakpoint. Measured 2026-10-21 on r1_S4_10x10_dense_1 (31 queries, caching on): Opus 5.5 read 85% of its input from cache on both the sync and the lockstep batch path (92-93% by the last query, each query reading exactly what the previous one wrote); Kimi K3 read 89% over 25 queries. Opus: the fleet run uses Message Batches with batch_cache_ttl=1h (the default; R1 lockstep rounds p50 7 min, p90 42 min, 2.4% over 1 h); a local run uses the sync API with cache_ttl=5m (the default; measured sync latencies 3-61 s). GPT-6 Astra: enable_prompt_cache=true selects explicit breakpoints; left off, OpenAI's implicit mode writes the whole prompt every query and reads none (about 1.25x uncached). Astra caching is NOT verified live (the OpenAI key returned 401): run a two-query check on it before launch. Kimi K3: implicit prefix cache on Moonshot's default 5m tier, which still hit with start-to-start query gaps up to 8.9 min; prompt_cache_ttl=1h is available but doubles the write price ($6/M vs $3/M) for no measured gain.
